---
title: Data sources
description: Where each OmicIDX table comes from, how often it refreshes, and which public file it lands in.
---

Each source is extracted on its own schedule. A nightly build then publishes
whatever has been extracted so far, so one slow source never holds up the rest.

| Source | Upstream | Extract cadence | Public files |
|---|---|---|---|
| NCBI SRA | [SRA mirroring XML](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/reports/Mirroring/), plus `SRA_Accessions.tab` | daily | `sra_studies`, `sra_samples`, `sra_experiments`, `sra_runs`, `sra_accessions`; `sradb/*` |
| NCBI GEO | GEO SOFT records via E-utilities and `acc.cgi`, one calendar month at a time | daily (current month re-fetched) | `geo_series`, `geo_samples`, `geo_platforms`, `geo_series_with_rnaseq_counts`; `geometadb/*` |
| NCBI BioSample | [`biosample_set.xml.gz`](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/biosample/) full dump | daily | `biosamples` |
| NCBI BioProject | [`bioproject.xml`](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/) full dump | daily | `bioprojects` |
| NCBI PubMed | [PubMed baseline and update files](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/) | hourly check for new files | `pubmed_articles` |
| NCBI Taxonomy | [`taxdump.tar.gz`](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/taxonomy/) | weekly | none: used to resolve organism names |

Every table is one Parquet file: `<name>.parquet` at the top of a release, or
`sradb/<name>.parquet` / `geometadb/<name>.parquet` for the compatibility
tables.

## Notes per source

- **SRA:** NCBI publishes full and incremental mirror files. OmicIDX loads them in order and keeps the latest version of each record. `sra_accessions` is NCBI's accession table (status, dates, relationships for every SRA accession).
- **GEO:** records are fetched one month at a time, by last-update date. The current month is re-fetched every night because it keeps growing, and the previous month is fetched again after it ends so its last days are complete. `geo_series_with_rnaseq_counts` lists the series for which NCBI provides computed RNA-seq count matrices.
- **BioSample and BioProject:** NCBI publishes these as single full dumps, so each night replaces the previous load.
- **PubMed:** the annual baseline plus the daily update files. New files are picked up within the hour and published in the next nightly build. `pubmed_articles.parquet` is large (about 37 GB), so filter it in place rather than downloading it.
- **Organism names:** NCBI Taxonomy renames organisms, and GEO updates its records to match without changing their last-update date. Organism names in `geo_series`, `geo_samples`, `sra_samples`, `biosamples` and the matching `sradb/` and `geometadb/` tables are therefore the *current* NCBI Taxonomy scientific name for the record's taxonomy ID (merged IDs are followed). The name as originally submitted is kept in a matching `*_as_submitted` column (for example `sample_organism_as_submitted`). If a taxonomy ID is unknown, the submitted name is used. `geo_platforms` has no taxonomy ID, so platform organisms stay as submitted.
- **EBI BioSamples:** extracted daily into the internal lake (by update date, from 2021-01-01), but not published yet.

## Compatibility tables

- **`sradb/`** (`study`, `sample`, `experiment`, `run`, `sra`, `run_with_study`, `rnaseq_runs`, `wgs_runs`, `human_runs`, `mouse_runs`): SRAdb-style names and columns. Legacy columns that are always empty are dropped. Modern cross-references (BioProject, GEO, PubMed) are added.
- **`geometadb/`** (`gse`, `gsm`, `gpl`, `gse_gsm`, `gse_gpl`, `geo_supplemental_files`): GEOmetadb-style tables.

Row counts for every published table are in each release's `manifest.json`.
